subject: Residency assurance, PII flow & region-pinning approach
messages:

Subject: Residency assurance, PII flow & region-pinning approach

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and three asks so we can align internal stakeholders at WellPath: 

Call recap (very short):
- WellPath will accept Redwood hosted inference but requires US-only residency for PII payloads; non-PII telemetry can cross regions.
- You asked about cross-region failover and whether backups (snapshots/logs) ever leave the US in our default config.
- SLA target discussed: 99.9% uptime, RTO goal 30 min for primary region failover.

Three asks / next steps:
1) Could you confirm which data you classify as PII vs telemetry for our compliance docs? (sample mapping file would be ideal)
2) We attached a proposed PII data-flow diagram and two region-pinning options (Option A=US-only for PII; Option B=US-primary with cold backups in EU for non-PII). Please review and mark preferred and any hard constraints.
3) If you need an explicit contractual commitment about backups never leaving the US for PII, let us know and we can loop Legal/Contracts to draft specific language.

Notes on technical behavior (short):
- Model inference requests flagged as PII will be routed to the US-only VPC endpoints; KV caches and prefix caches are scoped to the pinned region.
- Cross-region failover is supported via warm-standby, but the warm-standby cluster will only receive non-PII synced state unless you opt into cross-region replication for PII (requires Data Processing Addendum/controls).
- Audit/log shipping: application logs (redacted) can be forwarded to your Splunk instance in any region per config; raw request logs with PII are retained in the pinned region by default.

Attachments: wpl-pii-data-flow-diagram.pdf, region-pinning-options-compare.xlsx, wpl-ma-template-redwood-clauses.docx

Proposed immediate next step: can we aim to have your sample mapping and a preferred option by Thu 11 Mar? That will let us prepare a short SOW addendum and a proposed contract clause.

Thanks — I’ll be available all week for a quick follow-up call.

Best,

Thanks Irene — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from Security/Product: 

1) PII definition: for our initial pass, PII = patient identifiers (name, MRN, DOB, SSN), protected health information (PHI elements), and any free-text that contains PHI. Non-PII = model-generated metadata, telemetry, anonymized aggregated insights. We will share an exported sample mapping later today.

2) Backups: must confirm — we need backups and snapshots of PII to remain in the US. We can accept encrypted copies to a customer-controlled GCS bucket in the US only.

3) Failover behavior: product prefers warm-standby for faster RTO, but Security insists warm-standby not contain PII replicas outside US; we are open to a configuration where warm standby has a sanitized state (no raw PII), which could be acceptable. Can Redwood confirm technical feasibility and whether that imposes latency/SLO tradeoffs?

Final: we will send the mapping and a redline to the MA clause by EOD Wed. If possible, schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra/ops (Karthik) for Thu morning.

Olivia

Subject: RE: Residency assurance, PII flow & region-pinning approach

Olivia — thanks for the clarifications and for sending the sample mapping. Quick technical responses below (keeping it short for Security):

- US-only backups for PII: yes, we can ensure that snapshot exports containing PII are written only to a customer-controlled US GCS/Azure Blob. We support encrypted snapshots with KMS keys you control (bring-your-own-key).

- Warm-standby with sanitized state: feasible. Two recommended approaches: 
  a) Warm-standby without PII: replicate model binaries, embeddings indexes, and non-PII caches; omit user payloads and KV entries marked as PII. This keeps RTO low (minutes) but requires application-level idempotency handling on failover because missing PII state must be re-hydrated or requested.
  b) Cold-standby + journaled rehydration: keep journal of non-sensitive ops in standby, bring up a US-only recovery instance to apply journals on failover — longer RTO (~1–2 hours) but guarantees no PII leaves US.

- Latency/SLO tradeoffs: option (a) is the lower RTO; additional per-request rehydration can add ~100–300ms worst-case to first request after failover depending on sample sizes. Option (b) increases RTO but preserves the stricter isolation.

I attached a short matrix (region-pinning-options-compare.xlsx) with recommended defaults for healthcare customers. Also linking a short runbook template we can adapt.

Proposed next: Thu 11 Mar 09:30 PT technical sync (30 min) with your infra and security to validate the sanitized-warm standby approach. I can invite our infra lead and Monica will join to take notes on contract implications.

-Karthik
